title: Credit and Collections Desk Guidance — Disconnection Postponements under Medical and Life-Support Protections
content:
**Entitlement.** While a written disconnection notice is pending, an active protection under Medical and Life-Support Protections entitles the customer to a postponement of the protection's postponement length, starting as the protection's start rule provides. Postponements are granted only while the certification is active.

**Limits.** Within any 12 months, no more than one plus the protection's permitted renewals postponements, and no more than the protection's most postponement days in any rolling 12 months, are granted. A renewal requires a new practitioner form where the protection requires a new form for every renewal or recertification.

**Effects.** A postponement rescinds the pending notice, and where the protection requires a new written notice after a postponement, any later disconnection needs a new written notice. A payment arrangement is offered with every postponement. A postponement never reduces the balance owed.

## How the 12-month limits are measured

The measurement window is the 12 calendar months ending on the handling date. Within it, for the service agreement concerned:

- the **count** is the number of postponements whose first day falls in the window;
- the **days** are the sum, over those postponements, of the days from the first day through the last day of each, both days included.

A postponement is granted only where, with it included, the count stays within one plus the permitted renewals and the days stay within the most postponement days in any rolling 12 months.

## What is recorded

Each postponement granted is recorded with the written disconnection notice it postpones, its first day, its last day and the date it was granted. The pending notice is rescinded by the postponement, with the first day of the postponement as the date of the rescission.

## The condition of an active certification

The certification's status is read from the company's record of that certification before the postponement is granted. Only the active status satisfies it; a certification that is pending certification, denied, expired or withdrawn does not.

## Hypothetical cases

Figures used: a protection with a 30-day postponement, 2 permitted renewals and 90 days in any rolling 12 months; handling date 15 September; window 16 September of the previous year through 15 September.

| Postponements already in the window | Days already in the window | Requested postponement | Count with it | Days with it | Granted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0 | 30 days | 1 | 30 | yes |
| two of 30 days | 60 | 30 days | 3 | 90 | yes |
| three of 30 days | 90 | 30 days | 4 | 120 | no |

In the second and third rows the requested postponement follows a first one and is a renewal; where the protection requires a new form for every renewal or recertification, as all six protections do, the renewal requires a new practitioner form.

A postponement of 30 days requested on 1 June starts that day and runs through 30 June. The pending notice is rescinded; a disconnection after 30 June needs a new written notice, and the balance owed is unchanged by the postponement.
